doc.title: Nicki Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 2, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: How European and Japanese tours are booked years ahead
summary: European tours are booked by musicians and networks every other year, while Japan requires a promoter.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: And the fact that you mentioned that some tours abroad may book you two years in advance, so you have to like extrapolate do I want to do that in two years. It’s almost impossible to say.

Yeah, it is impossible to say, except that’s how a lot of the European promoters do things. They want you every other year. You know it’s more annuals over here. Over here it’s been more annual gigs, annual parties, annual things. But it doesn’t mean you can’t go to Europe but you have to go to Europe with band A, and then in the in between years you’re with the other groupings, you know what I mean? It’s complicated. They have a way of working it out. And these are all musicians mostly booking these gigs. Not agents. Networks. And you know some promoters, a few. And in Japan you cannot really go to Japan without a good promoter. You need a promoter for there. The language thing is just © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-
too difficult. So Japan always a promoter, Europe not necessarily. Musicians book it. But they are two years apart, the tours.
